newsitem.title: USA: Portugal lengthens patent life, trade row over - US.
newsitem.headline: Portugal lengthens patent life, trade row over - US.

text.p: Portugal and the United States settled a World Trade Organization dispute on Thursday, following Portugal's decision to extend the lifetime of existing patents, the U.S. trade representative's office announced.
The trade representative's office said Portugal had agreed it was obligated under new world trade rules to grant an extension of at least 20 years to patents already in force at the start of 1996.
Portugal revised its patent laws in 1995 to apply the new rules to patents issued in the future.
Several U.S. firms complained they would be deprived of significant income if the longer term was not allowed.
The U.S. trade representative's office took the complaint to WTO on April 30.
Acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky said the United States welcomed Portugal's "recognition of its WTO obligation and its implementation of those obligations."

Resolution of the dispute was mentioned earlier this week in an annual report on U.S. action to enforce trade laws. A Barshefsky aide said the United States formally advised Portugal of its acceptance of terms on Thursday.
